newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Freer trade costs Brazil industry $18 bln - report.
newsitem.headline: Freer trade costs Brazil industry $18 bln - report.

text.p: Brazil's policy of reducing import tariffs to encourage freer trade cost domestic industry nearly $18 billion in three years, a newspaper said on Saturday.

A study drawn up by the Ministry of Industry and Commerce estimated Brazilian manufacturers lost $17.7 billion to imported goods between 1993 and 1996, equivalent to 25.8 percent of industrial sales during the period, Jornal do Brasil said.
The study, which comes amid growing concern over Brazil's expanding trade deficit, suggested that the government consider measures to slow down the flow of imports.
"The correction of the trade balance in the medium term will not just depend on increasing exports," the document said.

For decades, Brazil protected its industry with stiff import tariffs and enjoyed regular trade surpluses. But tariffs have been cut steadily since 1990 in an attempt to make local manufacturers more competitive and reduce inflation.
As a result, Brazil's trade surpluses have turned into deficits, with last year's shortfall of $5.54 billion expected to grow to about $11 billion in 1997.

Faced with the flood of imports, Brazilian industry grew by 3.7 percent a year between 1993 and 1996, compared with 4.4 percent for the economy as a whole, the ministry's report said. The study also said 450,000 jobs were lost in Brazil's manufacturing sector between 1990 and 1995.

The document will serve as a "reference for the organisation of initiatives and actions by the Brazilian government," the newspaper quoted Francisco Dornelles, the minister of industry and commerce, as saying.
